officials.name: Carlos Bailey
officials.bio: As an attorney with over a decade of experience, Carlos Bailey has fought against racial injustice, employment discrimination, and has lent his voice to those who would have otherwise gone unheard. He opened the Bailey Law Firm of Southern Kentucky, PLLC in 2011, focusing on immigration, criminal, and civil litigation. A Bowling Green native, he graduated from Warren Central High School and Western Kentucky University, and currently serves on the Light of Chance Board.

officials.name: Dana Beasley-Brown
officials.bio: Dana Beasley Brown was elected to the City Commission in November 2018. She works at Bowling Green Junior High in the Youth Services Center, supporting kids and their dreams. Commissioner Beasley-Brown is committed to stewarding the city's current growth and ensuring a legacy for future generations.

officials.name: Melinda Hill
officials.bio: Melinda Hill brings more than thirty years’ experience designing and implementing programs for Fortune 500 Companies, a major local bank and governmental agencies. She has eight years’ experience providing senior leadership in accomplishing the goals of state and local governments and is particularly effective in the organization of new strategies and communicating these with all levels of the organization. Currently, Ms. Hill serves as Executive Director of CASA of South Central Kentucky.

officials.name: Sue Parrigin
officials.bio: Sue Parrigin brings decades of leadership and management experience from owning and operating her own business to working at Western Kentucky University. Dr. Parrigin is very active in our community serving on many boards and commissions. She is a 2017 retiree from Western Kentucky University and is currently employed as a Leadership Development Consultant.

officials.name: Todd Alcott
officials.bio: Todd Alcott is a JROTC teacher at Warren East High School and a retired Lt Colonel from the U.S. Air Force, having served over 21.5 years globally, including as Chief of Resilience for the Air Force at the Pentagon. He holds a Bachelor of Science from WKU and a Masters of Info Mgt from the University of Phoenix.

officials.name: Brian Painter
officials.bio: Commissioner Brian Painter was first elected District 1 Commissioner in November 2010 and is currently serving his fourth term. He enjoyed a professional career in hydrogeology and was a small business owner. He holds a Bachelor of Science from Northern Kentucky University and a Master of Science from Ohio University.

officials.name: Geoff Besecker
officials.bio: Commissioner Geoff Besecker was first elected District 2 Commissioner in November 2018 and is currently serving his second term. He recently retired after 28 years as a National Board Certified teacher at Campbell County High School, where he coached varsity baseball and chaired the Social Studies Department. He is actively involved in community initiatives, serving as president of the Campbell County Education Foundation and the Campbell County Kiwanis Club.

officials.name: Tom Lampe
officials.bio: Commissioner Lampe was elected District 3 Commissioner in November 2014 and is currently serving his third term. He is Vice President of New Sales Development with Hub International, an employee benefits consulting and insurance services firm.

officials.name: Steve Pendery
officials.bio: Judge/Executive Pendery has served as the elected Judge/Executive of Campbell County for 28 years. Prior to this, he served the City of Fort Thomas for 15 years as both Mayor and Councilman. He also co-owned his family's local small business, Pendery Insurance and Risk Management Group.

officials.name: David Voegele
officials.address: 100 West Jefferson Street La Grange, KY 40031
officials.bio: I am the Judge-Executive, or ‘county judge’, as the position is known. The county judge is the chief administrative officer of county government. The judge-executive does not conduct trials or act as a judge in the sense of a judge and jury, but rather presides at Fiscal Court.
